messages.author: b5e081313b0902ca
messages.subject: Error in matrix product indexing
parts:
Hi all,

I have trouble performing matrix products in Nimble. If I have to perform the product between two matrices X %*% B, this fails if the second dimension of X (and the first dimension of B) is 1, throwing the error:

Error in model$X[1:100, 1:1] %*% model$beta[1:1, 1:10] : non-conformable arguments

I have tried adding the argument drop=F to X and beta, but this leads to another error

Error in addMissingIndexingRecurse(code[[i]], dimensionsList) : inconsistent dimensionality provided for node 'X'

One way to code it up is to either explicitly doing the product via for loop, or to hard code an if(p == 1)..

Is there a cleaner way to make this run with a single line?

This is the example code:

nimbleCodeRegr <- nimbleCode({
 
  for(j in 1:S){
    for(k in 1:p){
      beta[k,j] ~ dnorm(0, 1)
    }  
  }
 
  Xbeta[1:n, 1:S] <-
    (X[1:n,1:p] %*% beta[1:p,1:S,drop=F])[1:n,1:S]  

  for(i in 1:n) {
    for(j in 1:S){
     
      y[i,j] ~ dnorm(Xbeta[i,j], sd = sigma)
     
    }  
  }
 
})

n <- 100
p <- 1
S <- 10
X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p)

constants <- list(n = n,
                  p = p,
                  S = S,
                  X = X,
                  sigma = 1)

MCMCsamples <-
  nimbleModel(
    code = nimbleCodeRegr,
    constants = constants,
    inits = list(beta = matrix(0, p, S)))


Alex

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Error in matrix product indexing
parts:
Hi Alex,
Thanks for the question and sorry for the delay in providing support here.
Situations with an index vector that reduces to a scalar are a rough part of nimble that will one day become better.
I also notice that, as written, if you are going to use default MCMC samplers on this model, each beta[k,j] will be sampled separately, but then all of Xbeta[1:n, 1:S] and all of the y[i, j] will be be recomputed when in fact only the Xbeta involving beta[k,j] should need to be recomputed, so you may want to consider writing the model to allow each Xbeta element to be a node. (Alternatively, you might be planning to have elements of beta[k,j] sampled in blocks, in which case there would be less redundant computation.) There are some ways it wouldn't scale up as well if you are looking to increase the size of the problem, but for moderate sizes it should result in (potentially much) faster (univariate) sampling by avoiding redundant computation. Back to your original question, one way to get different model variants from the same code is with definition-time if-then-else.  These are if-then-else blocks in model code that are evaluated *once*, when the model is created, resulting in different model variants when created with different constants (or R variables found by scoping in the R environment).  Below is an example if I also rewrite your model as noted.
HTH!
Perry

nimbleCodeRegr <- nimbleCode({
  for(j in 1:S){
    for(k in 1:p){
      beta[k,j] ~ dnorm(0, 1)
    }
  }

Xbeta[i,j] <- inprod(X[i, 1:p], beta[1:p, j])
      }
    }
  } else {

}
    }
  }
  for(i in 1:n) {
    for(j in 1:S){
      y[i,j] ~ dnorm(Xbeta[i,j], sd = sigma)
    }
  }
})

n <- 100

S <- 10
X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p)

constants <- list(n = n,
                  p = p,
                  S = S,
                  X = X,
                  sigma = 1)

nimbleModel(
    code = nimbleCodeRegr,
    constants = constants,
dimensions = list(X = dim(X), beta = c(p, S)),
inits = list(beta = matrix(0, p, S)))
